nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Fig trees of the forest. Their fruit is a staple for forest birds and primates; Wikipedia lists figs as a key food of the black-casqued hornbill.

nodes.name: African ebony & relatives
nodes.desc: Diospyros trees recorded repeatedly in the park area by GBIF. Their fleshy fruit is food for forest animals.

nodes.name: Gilbertiodendron
nodes.desc: Legume canopy trees that Wikipedia names among the characteristic trees of Sapo National Park.

nodes.name: Forest floor herbs
nodes.desc: Understorey herbs of the shaded forest floor, recorded in the park area. Herbs and ferns are food for ground browsers such as the pygmy hippo.

nodes.name: African forest elephant
nodes.desc: Eats bark, leaves and fruit and spreads seeds in its dung, sometimes over 5 km. Wikipedia calls it the megagardener of the forest.

nodes.name: Pygmy hippopotamus
nodes.desc: Forages at dusk on herbs, ferns, shoots and fallen fruit. Camera traps confirmed it in Sapo in 2008. Liberia holds most of the wild population.

nodes.name: Maxwell's duiker
nodes.desc: A small forest antelope that is locally abundant in Sapo and well recorded here. It feeds on leaves and fruit.

nodes.name: Bay duiker
nodes.desc: A forest duiker that is locally abundant in Sapo and the most recorded duiker in the park area.

nodes.name: Diana monkey
nodes.desc: Endangered monkey of the canopy. Eats mainly fruit, blossoms and leaves, plus some insects. Leopards, crowned eagles and chimpanzees prey on it.

nodes.name: Western red colobus
nodes.desc: A leaf-eating canopy monkey recorded in the park area. It is hunted by chimpanzees in other West African forests.

nodes.name: Black-casqued hornbill
nodes.desc: About 90 percent fruit, with figs and oil palm fruit as staples. An important seed disperser of forest trees.

nodes.name: Red river hog
nodes.desc: A forest pig that forages for fruit, roots and plants. GloBI has a record of it feeding on forest elephant.

nodes.name: Western chimpanzee
nodes.desc: The most recorded mammal in the park area, with a population estimated at 500 to 1,640. Eats fruit and hunts monkeys such as colobus.

nodes.name: African civet
nodes.desc: An omnivore eating fruit, small animals, insects and carrion. Its latrines may help spread seeds.

nodes.name: Palm-nut vulture
nodes.desc: Unusually for a raptor it eats mostly fruit, but also takes crabs, fish and carrion. GloBI has a record of it feeding on a buffalo.

nodes.name: African leopard
nodes.desc: The top mammal predator of Sapo. In African rainforests it mostly eats duikers and primates, and it also scavenges.

nodes.name: Crowned eagle
nodes.desc: A forest eagle whose most common prey is monkeys. It also takes duikers.

nodes.name: Seasonal rainfall
nodes.desc: Wet season from May to October and dry season from November to April set the rhythm of fruiting and growth.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Canopy trees about 25 m high intercept most of the light, leaving the forest floor shaded.

nodes.name: Swamps & rivers
nodes.desc: Swamp and seasonally flooded forest make up about a quarter of the park, with the Sinoe River on its west side. Home to the pygmy hippo.

nodes.name: Forest soil
nodes.desc: Soil holds the nutrients recycled from fallen leaves and dead animals.

nodes.name: Fungi, termites & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
